as_told.title: Bill Gunston: Brown's work went into the B-2

plain: Nick Cook is a journalist who has written about secret aircraft research. He tells the podcast host Jesse Michels about an article by Bill Gunston, a British aviation writer. Cook says Gunston worked out that the B-2, an American stealth bomber, was too heavy for its engines to give the performance claimed for it. The idea is that it might be getting a hidden boost from electrogravitics, a claimed way of using electric charge to push against gravity, linked to the inventor Townsend Brown. He names the magazines Military Power and Air International. In a later episode Cook tells it again, saying simply that the B-2's numbers did not add up. Michels also repeats it, saying Gunston was sure Brown's work went into the B-2, and dating the article to 2000 in Air International.
